answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to stake a small, slashable bond locked behind a crystal-clear public record, so spinning up thousands of fake agents becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation should then grow like a trellis: verifiable work history climbs slowly and cannot be bought in bulk, while a velvet-gloved rate limit throttles brand-new accounts until they prove real contributions. Cheap identities stay worthless; proven ones earn trust.
